title: Micropatches released for Windows Power Dependency Coordinator Elevation of Privilege (CVE-2026-69459)
content_md: September 2026 Windows Updates brought a patch for CVE-2026-69459, a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Power Dependency Coordinator, allowing a non-admin local user on the computer to elevate themselves to Local System. The vulnerability was found by two anonymous researchers who used it at the TyphoonPWN 2026 competition. Subsequently, SSD published a technical analysis of this issue, which allowed us to reproduce the issue and create patches for legacy Windows systems. The Vulnerability The vulnerability is a heap buffer overflow in the Component Resource Manager (CRM) state-monitor code of PsmServiceExtHost.dll. This module is loaded by Windows Power Dependency Coordinator running as Local System. A low-privileged local user can reach the vulnerable function through the documented power-settings API and overflow a fixed-size buffer, causing a memory corruption that can lead to arbitrary code execution. Microsoft’s Patch Microsoft fixed this issue by adding a check to confirm that the length of a value provided by the caller exactly matches the expected length - and abandons the call if this fails.
